issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-history). §2.7's support step (6) (b) (iii) (base l.2601-2605) makes an enceinte's trace cross a standing raised way 'through one station on the deck at its level — the one nearest where the trace would cross, the trace bent along the deck to pass through it, the station never moved'. A locked or pinned one is crossed the same way at generation (l.2592-2593). §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l.10593), V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s second bullet (V06 l.1596-1598) and V09's line say the same, with no else. Two reachable cases have no such station. (1) None at deck level: (2) gives n = max(1, round(L ÷ p)) spans and n − 1 interior stations (l.2533-2534), so a raised way shorter than 1.5 p has none (under 12-22 m masonry, 6-12 m timber; V11 §3.24.2). Examples: a drawn short raised way, a short elevated link or viaduct. Nor does one whose every interior station is on a ramp or a stair, which (6) never takes. (2) The nearest is already another enceinte's crossing station: an epoch contraction or re-anchored stretch, or a second hand `drawWall`, within p ÷ 2 of a standing crossing. (3)'s 'each taking the nearest interior station not yet taken' (l.2548-2550) holds only at generation, so two bands would share one support whose `supports` entry 'reads its stretch's `condition`' — of two stretches. (b) forbids adding a station. The ramps, stairs and feet are a reservation, only a way or a channel may pass under a span, and V06 says 'a trace never waits for a raised way' (V06 l.1603). So builders would add a station, pass the wall under a span, refuse, or share the station. No bar runs either case: T110-2 (4) and T-V6-47 cross multi-span raised ways at one crossing.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (b) (iii), after 'the one nearest where the trace would cross', add: 'and not already another trace's crossing station; where the raised way holds no such station — a single span (n = 1), every interior station on a ramp or a stair, or every one taken — the trace takes none: it is bent past the nearer foot (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`; the other where that foot lies on the arena's outer ring), clear of its ramp or stair and the under-deck strip, and crosses the part-0 way that leaves that foot, where one does, at a ground gate by §4.2 S3 (4)'s gate law. The raised way stands wholly on one side of the trace, nothing of it changed, reported (V06's wall report at an epoch; the dry run's line for a hand edit)'. At generation (a)'s 'else one added' stands. Ends: (1) determinism: §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` outcome cell adds '; where it holds no untaken station on the deck at its level, the trace bent past its nearer foot, a ground gate on the way beyond it (§2.7's support step (6) (b) (iii))'. (2) V06: §3.7.6 (5)'s second bullet adds the same clause. (3) V09: `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` gains words for the bend past the foot, ending with `button.showWhy`. (4) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (4) adds 'a hand `drawWall` across a declared one-span masonry viaduct, and an epoch contraction whose new ring meets an aqueduct within p ÷ 2 of the old ring's crossing station: the first bent past the nearer foot with a ground gate on the way beyond it, the second through the next untaken station; in both, every station, key, span and state of the raised way unchanged but that station's support'.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-vault-village): a village palisade across a `vault` span has two outcomes in two texts. §2.7's support step (6) (b) makes 'the under-deck strip of each `vault` span … a reservation on ground part 0 for every later way, trace, strip …', with the palisade listed among the ways of crossing 'the rest of its under-deck strip' (base l.2597-2600). Yet (iv) says the palisade 'abuts each support standing in its band and passes beneath every span' (l.2608-2609). V07 §3.5a (4) agrees with (iv): 'The trace passes beneath a span as an ordinary stretch' (V07 l.1600-1601). §4.13's `wall` row names only supports (l.8981). A `vault` span stands at the village rungs: `span.vaultCap` is 10 at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE (V11 l.3975), and V07 §3.5a (7) registers V04's arch-vault source at every village rung. A span crossing the perimeter's band is not 'wholly on hinterland faces', so `country` does not keep it open. Each `vault` span 'holds one arch vault at grade' (l.2635-2636): a chamber with walled-up arch mouths. So VS3's palisade, laid at a village derivation around a declared raised way (V07 §3.5a (1)), has two outcomes on one case: it runs through the arch vault's chamber (base (iv), V07 (4)), or it stops at a reserved strip and leaves the line open (base (b)'s reservation). T-V7-48 ('the palisade abuts each standing support in its band') runs no `vault` span. Two units state two outcomes for one case: MAJOR by R3-03 (b).
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (b) (iv) reads: '(iv) a village palisade (`VillagePlan.palisade`) abuts each support standing in its band and each arch vault of a `vault` span there — the trace ending at the vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole and closing the line between them — and passes beneath every `open` span, with no crossing station and no gate (V07 §3.5a (4))'. Ends: (1) V07: §3.5a (4)'s 'The trace passes beneath a span as an ordinary stretch' reads 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch and abuts a `vault` span's arch vault at its two arch mouths, never laid through the chamber (§2.7's support step (6) (b) (iv))'. (2) pipeline: §4.13's raised-way `wall` row reads 'a village palisade abuts its supports and its `vault` spans' arch vaults, the deck passing over with no gate'. (3) V07: T-V7-48 adds 'a declared viaduct with a `vault` span standing in the planned palisade's band: the palisade ending at the vault's arch mouths, the chamber whole, 0 palisade stretches inside an arch vault's footprint and no gap in the line'.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-river-raised x C-harbour-raised). R4-09's last support run (§2.7's support step (6) (a), base l.2589-2591): where a station 'this run can neither slide nor omit within `maxClearSpanM` and `maxPierM`', it 'keeps the place the earlier run gave it, and the S7 part it meets gives way in that batch — a strip, plaza or square cut round its ring, a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it'. A strip, plaza or square is a face, so 'cut round' defines it. A quay, pier or mole is a way: '`quay` ways along the waterfront … piers as `pier` ways … moles, breakwaters, quays and piers are `pier` / `quay` ways in S7's L1 batch' (§4.8 l.7717-7723). A castle path is a `path` way (l.2281). 'Ending at the ring and resuming beyond it' does not say whether the way stays one connected way, routed round the ring inside its platform, or is split into two antenna ends either side of a pier, which may cut a quay plot's, a pier head's or a water gate's only path (§5.3's network invariant). The case is common. A generated viaduct or aqueduct crossing a `quay`-banked river or canal in town sets its bank stations as near the water as (3) allows: the river's clear span is held at or under `maxClearSpanM` (masonry 30 m, timber 20 m), and a generated course past it drops. S7 then lays the `quay` ways along those banks. The last run finds each bank station in a quay's corridor, unable to slide landward (the river span would pass `maxClearSpanM`), into the water, or be omitted. §4.8's lead ('gives way round its ring', l.7592-7593) and §4.1's S7 row ('cut round its ring or ended at it', l.4932) add no rule for the way. T110-2 (3) counts '0 piers in a … quay, pier or mole' but no connectivity. Peers' VM-R4T-01 and VPC-R4-01 rule S5b and S5c ways and the intervallum lane and keep this wording.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (a): 'a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it' reads 'a quay's, pier's or mole's platform cut round its ring as a strip is, and its way — or a castle path — bent round the ring inside its own face, its corridor beside the ring no narrower than its class's least width, so the way stays one connected way; where that face cannot hold the bend, the way ends at the ring on the water side and re-joins its shore's nearest way on the land side by the shortest lawful link in that batch, so every plot, pier head and gate keeps a path (§5.3's network invariant)'. Ends: (1) pipeline: §4.8's lead and §4.1's S7 row read 'the S7 part it meets cut or bent round its ring (§2.7's support step (6) (a))'. (2) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (3) adds 'a CITY masonry viaduct across a `quay`-banked river at its clear-span bound: both bank stations kept, each quay cut round its ring, each quay's way one connected way round the ring, and every quay plot and water gate reached (§5.3)'.

issues.claim: §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2) pins the gates 'where the arterials cross the boundary (… k ≥ 2: every crossing of an S4, earlier-S5b or this stage's S5b arterial)', and step 3 keeps them 'never moving' (base l.5832-5838). A stage gate on a raised arterial is its raised gate (*Outer moats*, l.5882-5883). §2.7's support step (6) (a) (l.2578-2580) bends the trace along the deck through the nearest station at deck level where 'the trace would meet the raised way on a ramp or a stair'. T110-2 (2)'s fixture is exactly a stage-2 boundary falling on an S4 viaduct's ramp (l.18410-18412). The pin step neither cites (6) (a) nor says the pin is the crossing station. The bar fixes the outcome (the crossing station on the deck at its level), so a builder reconciles the two and nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2) adds, after the pinned-gate parenthesis: '— on a raised arterial the gate is its crossing station, pinned at the deck's station that §2.7's support step (6) (a) gives the crossing (never on a ramp or a stair, the pin moved along the deck to it before smoothing)'.
